messages:
sam_support: FYI cust752 opened a ticket — after we pinned them to variant redwood-open-7b-q8_0 they started getting embeddings of length 512 instead of 768. They only noticed after the pin.

sam_support: Quick paste from their API response: `{"model":"redwood-open-7b-q8_0","data":[{"embedding_length":512}]}` — they ran a batch of 10 and all vectors were 512.

jin_ml: Do we know whether the pin pointed to an alias that may map to a quantized variant? Alias/variant swap could produce different vec sizes if model families changed.

sam_support: They said they used the UI to pin specific version id `v2026-02-14-q8_0` (provided by customer). They believe it was an explicit pin not an alias.

lia_ops: Can we get the server-side request logs for that customer between the pin time and the first failed request? Need backend model_key, variant, and runtime node id.

mike_oncall: I'm pulling logs now. small grep to run: `grep cust752 /var/log/redwood/runtime/requests.log | tail -n 200` — look for fields `model_variant` and `embedding_size`.

eng_runtime_bot: Automated note: model routing service recorded fallback to variant redwood-open-7b-q4a on host rnode-34 for customer cust752 at 2026-03-15T18:04:12Z due to capacity constraints.

jin_ml: That lines up — q4a is a quantized variant with 512-dim outputs for this model family (we changed output projection size in that quantized export). If the routing service fell back to a different model artifact that had a different output head, that would explain the veclen change.

sam_support: Customer insists they pinned v2026-02-14-q8_0 though. Could fallback still happen for pinned models?

lia_ops: Pinned config should disable cross-variant fallback, but there's an exception when reserved capacity isn't available and the system is allowed to downgrade to cheaper capacity under `emergency_fallback` policy. Need to check their reserved/dedicated flags.

mike_oncall: I found the audit entry: pin applied at 2026-03-15T17:55:03Z by user cust752. At 18:04 the autoscaler reported node pressure and emergency_fallback was true for that tenant for a 2m window. There is an associated admin log: `fallback_allowed=true` (internal flag).

jin_ml: That would do it — pinned model + fallback_allowed means system still routed to a compatible variant to keep requests live. Unfortunately compatible in routing logic meant 'same semantic model' not 'same embedding head size'.

sam_support: Customer is asking for immediate mitigation — they want their previous 768-length vectors back. Suggestions?

lia_ops: Short-term: unpin them to force the earlier canary variant mapping to resume (if that mapping points back to the 768 artifact). Or toggle emergency_fallback=false for their tenant (requires ops escalation).

mike_oncall: Ops can flip `emergency_fallback=false` for cust752; that will cause requests to queue/return 503s instead of being routed to smaller-output variants. Do they prefer availability or consistent vector size?

sam_support: Customer prefers consistent shape — they'd accept some retries/throughput hit over corrupted embeddings. I'll ask if they want us to disable fallback.

jin_ml: For a longer-term fix we should: 1) update routing policy to consider `embedding_dim` when matching fallback variants; 2) add a validation header in SDK (`X-expected-embedding-dim`) that our runtime will enforce for pinned requests; 3) add telemetry alerts for sudden per-tenant embed-dim changes.

lia_ops: I'll open infra ticket to add `embedding_dim` as a routing constraint. Also adding a mitigation toggle in the console for customers to disable fallback for pinned models.

eng_runtime_bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-3387 — investigate embed-dim fallback behaviour + add routing constraint. Assigned to eng-runtime.

mike_oncall: For now I disabled fallback for cust752 at 2026-03-15T19:05:00Z. Please confirm with customer and run a small batch.

sam_support: I asked the customer to retry and they ran a 3-request test: response shows `embedding_length=768` now. Customer reports downstream pipeline back to normal. :relieved:

sam_support: Follow-up actions for internal tracking: - eng-runtime to ensure pinned+fallback semantics are explicit, - add per-tenant dim-change alerting, - docs note on pinning + emergency fallback.

jin_ml: I'll start a PR for the routing constraint change and add unit tests that simulate fallback candidates with mismatched projection heads.

lia_ops: I'll add a console toggle and update the audit workflow so ops approvals are logged when fallback is turned off.

mike_oncall: Marking thread for postmortem if we see more than 1 cust impacted in 24h.

sam_support: Thanks all — closing the support case pending the infra/eng fixes.

eng_runtime_bot: Postscript: added correlation log entry `fallback_reason=capacity` and `served_variant=redwood-open-7b-q4a` for the original requests.

sam_support: Leaving this here for handoff to eng-runtime and ops.
